deviations.title: PlaceObject2 flag bits: HasClipActions is 0x80 and Move is 0x01
deviations.retail_evidence: PROVEN: 97186 PlaceObject2 records (top-level + inside DefineSprite) in the 83 movies under output/gfx_movies. Parsed with 0x80 = HasClipActions: 97186/97186 consume exactly their tag body. Parsed with gfxforge's 0x01 = HasClipActions: 10225/97186 (only the 10225 records with neither bit set). Of the 86961 records with 0x01 or 0x80 set, 86961 parse only under the retail reading, 0 only under gfxforge's. (86959 records carry 0x01, 2 carry 0x80.) (Consistent with the published SWF spec bit order — INFERRED, spec not re-read in this pass.) Driver: scratch drivers/retail_scan.js.
deviations.rust_expectation: Writer sets 0x80 for clip actions, 0x01 for move; reader treats 0x80 as HasClipActions. Tests port suite.timeline.js:168 with the 0x80 assertion; decode tests use the retail_corrected fixture bytes.

deviations.title: Long tag header on short bodies must be preserved (lossless layer)
deviations.retail_evidence: PROVEN: 8415 top-level tags in the 83 movies use the long (0x3f + u32) header for a body < 63 bytes, plus 7208 more inside DefineSprite (total 15623; by code: {"2":1419,"12":2169,"26":3993,"32":80,"37":1019,"39":1749,"43":2309,"56":2035,"70":2,"71":34,"74":569,"75":8,"83":237}). Over the 69 unique-content files (shell/ duplicates removed): 6759 top-level + 5606 nested. Driver: scratch drivers/retail_scan.js, drivers/retail_scan2.js.
deviations.rust_expectation: gfx::tag records the header form per tag and re-emits it byte-identically. No gfxforge test exercises this; it needs new retail-identity tests (not from this ledger). Authoring output may keep gfxforge's short-form rule.

deviations.title: Raw GFX FileLength = actual size - 8
deviations.retail_evidence: PROVEN for the raw (uncompressed GFX) movies present: 3/3 (fanfare_new_contact.gfx 1292 vs 1300, fanfare_support_unlocked.gfx 1302 vs 1310, snatch_moment.gfx 3201 vs 3209). The 80 CFX movies instead store FileLength = full uncompressed length including the 8-byte header (offset just past the End tag; 80/80). Caveat: the 3 raw-GFX movies are exactly the 3 with ExporterInfo version 0x010f/0x010d flags 0x03 (see D4); no retail movie combines exporter 0x0207/flags 0x13 with raw GFX, so the retail_corrected fixture bytes (0x0207 + 0x13 + raw + len-8) are a combination not observed in retail. Also: every CFX movie inflates to more bytes than FileLength, with non-zero trailing bytes after the End tag (retail_scan2.json fileLenRows) — the lossless layer must preserve them. Driver: scratch drivers/retail_scan2.js.
deviations.rust_expectation: Rust raw-GFX writer emits total-8; Rust verifier accepts total-8 for raw GFX and FileLength == decompressed-through-End for CFX. Fixtures carry both forms (movie.gfxforge / movie.retail_corrected).

deviations.title: ExporterInfo flags = 0x13
gfxforge: js/codec/swf.js:72-76 (exporterInfo writes u16 version 0x0207, u32 flags 0, u16 0x000d, u8 0)
deviations.retail_evidence: PROVEN: first 9 body bytes of tag 1000 across the 83 movies: {"0702130000000d0000":80,"0f01030000000d0000":2,"0d01030000000d0000":1} — 80/83 are 07 02 | 13 00 00 00 | 0d 00 | 00; the other 3 (fanfare_new_contact, fanfare_support_unlocked, snatch_moment) are version 0x010f/0x010d with flags 0x03. The meaning of the flag bits is not established here.
deviations.rust_expectation: Authoring writer emits flags 0x00000013 with version 0x0207; codec round-trips whatever is present. Fixtures carry gfxforge (0) and retail_corrected (0x13).

deviations.title: compiler-baseline does not fail when an ok:false program compiles
deviations.retail_evidence: PROVEN (test logic): a program with ok:false that compiles, or throws, is never reported. At this commit tests/fixture.compiler-baseline.json has 54 entries, 0 with ok:false, 7 EXPR: entries — so the gap is latent.
deviations.rust_expectation: Rust test asserts byte equality for ok:true and a compile error for ok:false.

deviations.title: DefineButton must not be emitted by components
deviations.retail_evidence: PROVEN: tag 7 (DefineButton) and tag 34 (DefineButton2) occur 0 times across the 83 movies (top-level + nested; tag counts {"7":0,"34":0}). Consistent with docs/reverse_engineer/gfx_golden_set.md:19 and gfx_authoring_feature_spec.md:47-48,143.
deviations.rust_expectation: gfx::component never emits tag 7; gfx::tags codec still decodes/re-encodes DefineButton for identity. Fixtures from button()/menu() movies are marked retail_corrected_unavailable (no byte patch can produce the redesigned component).
